findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() performs file I/O with an unwrap on a fallible Result. The public function load_sensors exposes file-system access and panics on any read failure.
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> with a Read variant; replace unwrap() with .map_err(|e| SensorError::Read(e)) and make the function signature explicit about I/O.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on malformed numeric input. The unwrap discards a fallible Result from u32::parse.
findings.failure_mode: A single non-numeric value in any CSV line crashes the entire loader instead of returning a typed parse error for that record.
findings.fix: Replace .unwrap() with .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> so callers handle bad data.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds stdout I/O (logging) inside what should be pure parsing logic. This is hidden I/O in the data-construction path.
findings.failure_mode: Side-effecting I/O contaminates pure data parsing, breaks determinism, and makes the function不可testable without capturing stdout.
findings.fix: Move all printing/logging to the shell layer. The load_sensors function should only parse and construct domain values; callers decide what to log.

findings.problem: value: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16. Values above 65535 silently truncate to fit u16.
findings.failure_mode: A sensor value of 70000 becomes 4464 without any warning, corrupting domain data silently.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to catch out-of-range values with a typed error instead of silent truncation.

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the first element of a split Vec by index with no bounds check. If a line has fewer than 2 fields, this panics.
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one comma-separated field (or an empty line) causes an index-out-of-bounds panic instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Replace split().collect() + indexing with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) for two-field records, eliminating index and bounds checks entirely.

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the second element by index with no bounds check. Same unchecked access violation as parts[0].
findings.failure_mode: Same as above — a malformed line with fewer than two fields panics on index access.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) which yields (_name, value_str) tuple safely without any index or bounds access.

findings.problem: The Record struct uses pub name: String and raw primitives exposed publicly. Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can create a Record with an empty name, negative or out-of-range value, or any invalid combination without the type system preventing it.
findings.fix: Make fields private, provide a smart constructor or ParseError-returning parser, and consider newtyping name (e.g., SensorName) with validation invariants.

findings.problem: No bounded allocation with try_reserve exists. The function collects lines into Vec<String> via intermediate allocations with no input size cap and no try_reserve guard.
findings.failure_mode: A large or adversarial file triggers unbounded heap allocation with no domain cap, no checked capacity arithmetic, and no Allocation error for graceful handling.
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap/max lines first, then use Vec::new followed by values.try_reserve(cap).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)? before any pushes. Avoid intermediate Vec<String> — parse directly into Record.

residual_risk: Source-level review only. Multiple BLOCKER violations remain: hidden I/O (fs::read_to_string, println!), panic surfaces (two unwrap() calls), lossy cast (u32 as u16), unchecked indexing (parts[0], parts[1]), no typed error taxonomy, no bounded allocation with try_reserve, and raw primitives in domain type. Without running cargo gates, tests, or benchmarks, these defects are unmitigated. Delivery is blocked.
